The welcome-back window is `channels.registration.welcome-back-window`, default 24h (a nil value is set to 24h by LoadConfig); 0 turns the welcome-back message off so every account gets the greeting.

The greeting-length key is `channels.registration.greeting-max-length` (default 200 via LoadConfig), not `max-greeting-length`; `default.yaml` and `traditional.yaml` list `greeting-max-length: 200` under `channels.registration`.

For PRIVMSG-to-service commands marked unsplitFinalParam, servicePrivmsgHandler splits the message with splitRawFinalParam, which keeps the final parameter's internal and leading spaces, dropping only one separating space; the CHANSERV command form (serviceCmdHandler) still joins parsed params with single spaces.

`CS ENTRYMSG #channel REGULARS <text>` sets the welcome-back message, using the same founder/chanreg/admin permission check, freeze refusal, and GreetingMaxLength limit as the greeting; with no text (or only whitespace) it removes the welcome-back message. The welcome-back text is stored unmodified and is not recorded in the greeting history.

An account that joined a registered channel within `channels.registration.welcome-back-window` (default 24h) receives the channel's welcome-back message instead of the greeting; accounts without a login always get the greeting, and if no welcome-back message is set such a joiner gets no greeting.

`make test` runs go test and go vet with tags "i18n mysql postgresql sqlite" and with no tags, then `./.check-gofmt.sh`; `make smoke` runs `install` and then `ergo run --conf ./default.yaml --smoke`, which needs the installed `ergo` on PATH, so a freshly built binary outside GOBIN fails with "ergo: not found".

`default.yaml` and `traditional.yaml` both list `max-greeting-length: 200`, `max-notes: 25` and `max-note-length: 300` under `channels.registration`, so they load unchanged and show the defaults.
Before the channel-limits change, NOTE ADD in ChanServ had no maximum note length; the only limit was the number of notes per channel, a fixed constant maxChannelNotes = 10.

The channel limits are read from `channels.registration.max-greeting-length` (default 200), `max-notes` (default 25) and `max-note-length` (default 300) into `Config.Channels.Registration.MaxGreetingLength`, `MaxNotes` and `MaxNoteLength`; LoadConfig substitutes these defaults when a key is missing or 0.

Channel.Join flushes the joiner's ResponseBuffer after the JOIN, topic and names; a greeting sent with client.Send after that flush reaches every session of the joining client, including for SAJOIN.

ChanServ commands marked authRequired are refused for clients not logged into an account before the handler runs, so a chanreg oper with no account cannot use them; ENTRYMSG omits authRequired and checks the login itself, which lets chanreg opers use it without an account (verified live).

Services' NUH prefix (e.g. ChanServ!ChanServ@localhost) is a runtime value set at init and overridden by overrideServicePrefixes from the services hostname config; referencing the chanservService variable from code reachable from chanservCommands causes a Go initialization cycle, so the prefix is passed explicitly.

Inbound client lines longer than 512 bytes get ERR_INPUTTOOLONG (417) unless server.compatibility allowTruncation is set, so a user cannot submit 200 three-byte characters in one line (verified against a live test server).
Outgoing IRC lines longer than 512 bytes are truncated by ircmsg when serialized, so a server-built message must be split by the sender to avoid losing its end.
A registered channel's persisted registration includes its ChannelSettings, so a field added to ChannelSettings is saved and reloaded with the registration across restarts.
`ChanServ`'s services prefix is `ChanServ!ChanServ@localhost` unless a services hostname is configured; unsolicited service messages take this as their prefix.
